items.title: Live: US extend ceasefire with Iran, JD Vance cancels Pakistan trip
items.description: US President Donald Trump says he is extending the ceasefire with Iran. Follow live.

items.title: Trump says Iran's government 'seriously fractured' as he extends ceasefire
items.description: US President Donald Trump says he will hold off attacking Iran until Tehran's negotiating teams come up with a unified proposal for a peace deal.

items.title: What life is like for those trapped on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz
items.description: For months seafarers have been stranded in the Strait of Hormuz, tanker captain Raman Kapoor is speaking out about the fears and uncertainty of his crew.

items.title: The growing problem stopping Melbourne residents using their microwave
items.description: A power company warns that growing electricity demand is creating an undervoltage issue as Victoria's infrastructure struggles to keep up with the transition from gas.

items.title: Remote residents 'cooking from the inside' sue NT government
items.description: Residents of the Central Australian community of Papunya say the scorching hot outback summers are killing their people in unsafe housing. Now they’re suing the Northern Territory government to try to force change.

items.title: 500,000 Australians wait for end to 'limbo' as Butler readies NDIS plan
items.description: NDIS Minister Mark Butler must end the uncertainty half a million people have been living in when he announces changes to the nation's disability scheme, mental health advocates say.

items.title: In a split second, Keelie made the 'surreal' decision to reveal her abuse
items.description: As Australia marks Sexual Assault Awareness Month, experts and victim-survivors say sexual violence remains pervasive and under-reported.

items.title: Junior clubs and brain experts welcome NRL training changes
items.description: Junior rugby league clubs and neuroscientists have welcomed changes to address growing concerns around injuries but say more should be done to protect children.

items.title: Carpooling an 'effective solution' to fuel prices, so why aren't more doing it?
items.description: Despite fuel prices soaring in March, the number of vehicles travelling along a key carpooling lane in Sydney increased by just 1 per cent. A transport expert says more needs to be done to encourage people to share their commutes.

items.title: Off-the-plan homebuyer 'lives in her car' amid construction delays
items.description: Five years after signing contracts and paying their deposits, families say their lives have been put on hold as they wait to move into their "forever homes" in Newcastle.

items.title: Fourth man charged over alleged kidnapping murder of Chris Baghsarian
items.description: The 85-year-old's abduction triggered an 11-day search, with his remains later found near a golf course in Pitt Town, in the city's north-west.

items.title: Gift bags and cruise ship fallout part of Adelaide's COP31 considerations
items.description: A heavily redacted feasibility study into Adelaide's capacity to host the COP31 UN climate summit provides a fleeting glimpse into what was under consideration — including politically fraught floating hotels.

items.title: Japan to sell lethal arms in move away from post-war pacifism
items.description: Japan has overhauled its decades-long defence export rule, allowing the country to sell lethal weapons internationally amid rising global tensions.

items.title: 'It's been horrible': Your experiences with family estrangement
items.description: Our recent stories about the grief of family estrangement resonated strongly. Here is how some Australians have been affected by it.

items.title: Travel quiz: Grab your bags and see if you can beat our quiz
items.description: Which city is hosting the first game of the World Cup? What's the name of Egypt's currency?

items.title: The artworks we can't stop thinking about from the Adelaide Biennial
items.description: The legacy of nuclear testing, environmental degradation and more among the challenges facing Australia, as explored by artists in the Adelaide Biennial of Australian art.

items.title: What 100 years of Australian soil can tell us about our history and future
items.description: Far from brown dirt, the Australian National Soil Archive houses 100,000 soil samples — some a century old — that represent a slice through time of the ground beneath our feet.

items.title: Women's shelter funding welcomed, as most turned away
items.description: A women's shelter struggling to meet enormous demand says it will soon be able to almost double its capacity.

items.title: More uncounted votes discovered in SA a month after election
items.description: More uncounted votes have been discovered in two electorates a month on from the South Australian state election, and while the state's Electoral Commission says the ballots will not harm the "integrity" of the count, they have not said how many have been found.

items.title: Man jailed for mimicking shooting on bridge used in Bondi attack
items.description: A man who yelled antisemitic profanities while pretending to shoot at people from a pedestrian bridge used by the Bondi Beach terror attack gunmen has been sentenced.

items.title: Young benches ex-coach's son and fires assistant to start Dragons tenure
items.description: Dean Young names the first team of his tenure as Dragons coach, dropping Kyle Flanagan to the bench and sacking assistant and attack coach Michael Ennis.

items.title: 'I'd still be in jail': The rehab where women find hope after addiction
items.description: Guthrie House is one of the few residential rehabilitation services in NSW designed to help women with current involvement with the criminal justice system get back on track.

items.title: Sacked civil servant describes pressure to approve Mandelson as UK ambassador to US
items.description: The former head of the Foreign Office said there was "a very, very strong expectation" that Peter Mandelson "needed to be in post and in America as quickly as possible".

items.title: Paramedics unable to help bleeding mother for almost an hour, inquest hears
items.description: A paramedic tells an inquest she decided to wait for police back-up before attending to a woman who was actively harming herself in a Northern Territory domestic violence shelter.

items.title: Police allege trio used edged weapons, slingshot in 'violent incident'
items.description: A man remains in a critical condition in hospital, and three others have been charged by police, after a "violent" altercation in the remote Northern Territory community of Ngukurr.
